newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money up to 4.00 pct before month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money up to 4.00 pct before month-end.

text.p: German call money rates jumped as high as four percent in active Friday trading as liquidity conditions tightened unexpectedly, erasing all hopes for a tension free end of the month.
"We have seen rates as high as four percent today, and we are looking for more swings in rates before the day is over," a dealer said.

Today's rates, quoted between 3.50/4.00 percent, are a long way from Thursday's 2.90/3.00 percent rates, but traders said they had anticipated a sharp increase today when rates began nudging towards 3.25 percent on Thursday afternoon.

"You can forget all about a smooth end of month," a dealer added, reversing all earlier predictions that this month the liquidity situation had been calibrated so carefully that no swings would be seen.
But federal and state government borrowings, which will flow back into the market later, have complicated the situation, dealers said.
Additionally banks still do not know the Bundesbank reserve data, leaving them somewhat in the dark in terms of how much more money they need to hold to fulfil their month reserve targets.
Dealers predicted that the market would be forced to borrow considerable amounts of funds at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate.
"I don't think we can get by without taking on Lombard borrowings, even though we are pretty close to the reserve requirements," a dealer said.

Looking ahead however dealers largely expect a normalisation in rates in the coming days, saying today's swings would not last much longer. Even this afternoon dealers said the market could already be awash in more funds.
On Wednesday holdings at the Bundesbank stood at 38.7 billion marks, down from 40.4 billion marks on Tuesday.
The monthly average remains unchanged at 38.6 billion marks, while Lombard borrowings on Thursday stood at 300 million marks, up from 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was quoted at 4.00000 percent on Friday compared with 2.98792 percent on Thursday.
